sentences.text: Shri D. N. Shukla - Advocate for the applicant.
Shri S. M. Patel - Panel Lawyer for respondent.

Order 
This is second application filed by the applicant under Section 483 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 for grant of regular bail relating to FIR No.222/2024, dated 21.5.2024 registered at Police Station-Bhalumada, District-Anuppur (M.P.) for commission of offence punishable under Sections 304B, 498A and 34 IPC and Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
Applicant is in detention since 21.5.2024.

Applicant's first bail application was dismissed as withdrawn and not pressed vide order dated 1.8.2024 passed in M.Cr.C. No.32411/2024 with liberty to renew the prayer for bail after recording of evidence of material witnesses before the Trial Court.
2.
As per the prosecution story, on 05.5.2024, Radhika whose marriage was performed with Jamuna Prasad Kevat (son of the applicant) one year ago, committed suicide by hanging herself.
FIR was registered.

In NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:377 2 MCRC-47151-2024 the course of investigation, it revealed that she was being tortured & harassed by the applicant and other co-accused persons in connection with demand of Rs. 3 Lac cash and one motorcycle.
After investigation, charge-sheet has been filed.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant has not committed any offence.
She is innocent.
She has been falsely implicated.
She is the monther-in-law of the deceased.

It is further submitted that all material witnesses including parents of the deceased have been examined Jamuni Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103881251/
1 and allegations are against the husband of deceased.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
As material witnesses have been examined,
applicant, who is mother-in-law, may be released on bail, pending the trial.
4 On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer for grant of bail to the applicant.
5 . Applicant is mother-in-law.

Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case including the fact that material witnesses have already been examined and main allegations are against the husband of deceased, but without expressing anything on the merits of the case, I am of the view that it is a case in which further pre-trial detention of the applicant is not warranted.
Consequently, this bail application under Section 483 of BNSS, 2023 for grant of bail filed on behalf of applicant stands allowed.

6 It is directed that applicant - Jamuni Bai be released on bail on her furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:377 3 MCRC-47151-2024 thousand only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court, for her regular appearance before the trial Court during trial with a condition that she shall remain present before the concerned Court on all the dates fixed by it during trial.

She shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 480(3) of BNSS, 2023.
7.
This order shall be effective till the end of the trial.
However, in case of bail jump and breach of any of the conditions of bail, it shall become ineffective.
Certified copy as per rules.
(DINESH KUMAR PALIWAL) JUDGE mrs. mishra Jamuni Bai vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103881251/
